articles.title: Rust pattern matching: handle missing values without panics

images.alt: Four distinct capsules pass through an inspection instrument and travel along separate tracks to matching destinations.
images.caption: Inspect the alternative first, then choose the operation that belongs to that case.

images.alt: Some(0) maps to Zero, Some(5) to Positive, Some(-2) to Other integer, and None to Missing.
images.caption: The examples exercise four outcomes. The final unguarded present-value arm covers integers that fail earlier conditions.

images.alt: Matching token shapes enter the same keyed drawer before output cards are aligned for a report.
images.caption: Group by key during accumulation, then choose presentation order as a separate step.

images.alt: Updates rust 0 to 1, crab 0 to 1, rust 1 to 2, followed by the sorted report crab 1 and rust 2.

articles.title: Rust numeric safety: checked arithmetic and honest conversions

images.alt: A precision instrument sends an overflowing flow toward a safety gate, a circular return track and a capped reservoir.
images.caption: Rejecting, wrapping and clamping express different rules at the same numeric boundary.

images.alt: For u8 250 plus 10, checked_add gives None, wrapping_add gives 4, and saturating_add gives 255; narrowing 300 gives 44 or an error depending on the conversion.
images.caption: A numeric boundary needs an explicit policy. Build-profile defaults are not an application contract.

articles.title: Rust traits and generics: choose a clear dispatch boundary

images.alt: Two differently shaped measuring instruments share one connector and feed direct and selectable routes through an architectural interface.
images.caption: Share an operation where it helps callers; keep concrete storage and ownership decisions explicit.

images.alt: Generic concrete types flow through separate generic uses, while two implementations can be borrowed through one dyn Measure interface.
images.caption: Generics preserve concrete type information at the call boundary; a trait object supplies a common interface with dynamic dispatch.

articles.title: Rust text input: buffered reading without lost errors

images.alt: A paper ribbon passes through a buffered inspection station while malformed segments are retained in a separate tray.
images.caption: Keep access, decoding and validation as distinct stages, and retain enough information to explain a rejected record.

images.alt: Bytes pass through UTF-8 decoding, line processing and domain validation, with a read_line loop that clears its buffer and stops at zero bytes.
images.caption: These are conceptual stages. Text-reading errors and field-validation errors need separate handling.
